counterfactual_missing_items: No histopathologic confirmation of the cyst type
No alternative lesion such as a solid tumor or abscess
No direct diagnostic label beyond imaging and laryngoscopy
decisive_items: 20×20 mm round cystic mass at the base of the tongue
33×31×27 mm well-defined cystic lesion in the midline of the tongue base
complete pharyngeal airway obstruction during both inspiration and expiration
response.rationale: R5 directly identifies the causative base-of-tongue cystic lesion, which explains the airway obstruction and secondary OSA. R3 captures the OSA syndrome and polysomnography findings but describes a downstream consequence rather than the most likely underlying diagnosis. R2 and R4 are unrelated chronic comorbidities.

rejected.why: OSA is demonstrated by symptoms and PSG, but it is the complication of the base-of-tongue cyst rather than the most likely unifying diagnosis.
Diabetes is only an incidental medical history item and does not explain the tongue-base mass, airway obstruction, or OSA.
Hypertension is only an incidental medical history item and has no causal or diagnostic role in the presented lesion.
